newsitem.title: USA: U.S. grain crop seen in better shape than year-ago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grain crop seen in better shape than year-ago.

text.p: A survey of members attending the U.S. Feed Grains Council meeting showed the majority have crops that are in much better shape than one year ago, according to survey results released on Tuesday.

Of the 21 members of the group who returned the survey, 14 said their crop stands were in better-to-much better condition this year than one year ago. Ten said their crops were in about the same condition as this time in 1996, and three members said crop stands were worse-to-much worse.
The informal survey also showed results roughly in line with recent U.S. Agriculture Department reports estimating planted U.S. acreage this season.

Members of the feed grain council said their sorghum and barley plantings were down by 63 percent and 40 percent, respectively, compared to 1996. Meanwhile, soybean and corn plantings were up 66 percent and 33 percent, respectively.
When asked to estimate the 1997/98 average farm prices, respondents at the meeting gave forecasts on the low side of the USDA range of estimates.
The survey showed feed grain council members expected to see an average price of $2.33 per bushel for corn, compared to the USDA projected range of $2.25-$2.65.

Sorghum was expected to average $2.24 per bushel, according to feed grain council respondents, compared to USDA estimates of $2.00-$2.40. And barley was estimated to bring $2.22 per bushel this growing season, compared to USDA estimates of $2.10-$2.50.
